PullRequest.Title: sessions: Fix unified workspace picker flyout
PullRequest.Body: Fixes #336582 This fixes the unified Agents Window workspace picker flyout by: - restoring standard delayed submenu hover behavior while retaining click activation - making Enter on the Remote row open the submenu and focus its search field - preserving row-top alignment while shifting tall flyouts upward to use available viewport height - sizing the Remote flyout to its content with a search-friendly minimum and viewport clamping - showing full submenu descriptions on hover - tightening the Sessions-specific submenu chevron gutter Validation: - `npm run compile` - ESLint on the changed TypeScript files - ActionListWidget unit tests (116 passing) - WorkspacePicker unit tests (111 passing)

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the unified workspace picker and move the pointer across the Remote row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Picker progress requires synchronous construction of the in-memory item model and initial list layout. Hovering Remote now schedules submenu creation after the standard 500 ms delay; transient pointer crossings cancel before submenu DOM construction, so that work is off the critical path unless the pointer remains.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 10 Agents recents plus the service's cached, deduplicated VS Code recents (capped at 10), together with registered provider browse/manage actions and remote hosts. Submenu width measurement falls back to 380 px at 50 or more total items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Picker construction is synchronous. Submenu hover uses one replaceable timeout; moving to another row cancels the prior show, so there is no aggregate creation burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Agents recents come from profile storage and VS Code recents come from the service's cached _vsCodeRecentFolders array. On a cold history load the picker uses the currently available cache and is refreshed by the existing event; warm opens reuse the loaded cache. The diff changes neither keys, invalidation, misses, nor coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the hover scheduler, cancellation, history caps, and synchronous DOM layout path are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider counts and label lengths vary, but recent-history cardinality and the rendered submenu viewport are bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Removing submenuPointerIntent changes Remote hover from immediate synchronous submenu construction to delayed, cancellable construction, reducing eager UI work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Remote submenu by click or Enter and display it near the viewport edge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit activation synchronously creates the nested ActionListWidget, lays it out, measures row widths with DOM geometry reads, positions the panel, and focuses the nested widget for keyboard activation. No external boundary must complete before the submenu appears.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the effective remote submenu item count, while DOM rendering remains virtualized to the viewport. The new vertical calculation can expose up to the screen's worth of rows instead of one row; width remains viewport-clamped, and lists of 50 or more use the existing 380 px width shortcut.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One submenu widget exists at a time; showing another clears and disposes the previous per-submenu resources. Activation is synchronous and serialized on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The submenu consumes actions and filter items already assembled when the parent picker opened; it performs no cache lookup or refresh. Cold and warm behavior are therefore identical for this activation step.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: construction, computeListHeight, computeMaxWidth, geometry reads, viewport clamping, and list virtualization are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual row count and viewport size vary, but both the history source and visible DOM row count are bounded. Wider labels can increase the chosen internal width below 50 items, but do not add width-measurement passes compared with the capped pre-diff behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Enter adds this bounded work only on deliberate activation; click already performed it. Removing maxWidth changes the resulting width but not the existing measurement pass, and the vertical shift intentionally uses otherwise available viewport space without rendering an unbounded list.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filter or resize an open Remote submenu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Typing filters the already-created in-memory item list and requests a synchronous nested-list relayout. Window resize invokes the stored submenu layout function directly; neither path waits on external work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filtering and height recomputation scale linearly with the bounded submenu item set; rendered rows remain constrained to the available viewport.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Input events execute serially on the UI thread. The nested layout request is immediate, while resize observation for non-list hover content is animation-frame coalesced; this changed submenu uses the list path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Filtering operates on _allMenuItems and does not query or invalidate workspace history. There is no cold-cache retry or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: filter layout events and resize ownership are explicit in ActionListWidget.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rapid typing or resize frequency is device-dependent, but the diff adds only constant-time desired-height arithmetic to each existing layout and does not add a new observer or boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The changed geometry calculation does not add collection-wide DOM measurement or external work per event.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select a remote workspace after opening the submenu with the keyboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a separate child-row activation, the submenu action populates the existing parent item and dispatches selection. A disconnected provider connection and any local file existence validation are sequentially awaited before selection can finish; these operations are not performed merely by the newly supported Enter-to-open action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect the selected remote provider on demand
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when already connected; otherwise one call for the single selected workspace
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same call followed child selection after click or existing submenu keyboard navigation; the diff only lets Enter open the submenu.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the selected remote workspace action, but not submenu opening

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether a selected file-scheme workspace exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one exists call for the single selected file-scheme workspace
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same validation ran for remote submenu selections reached through existing pointer or ArrowRight activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks final selection validation, but not submenu opening

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected child produces at most one provider connection attempt and at most one file existence check. Browse actions similarly execute only the single selected provider action, not one call per listed workspace.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection is sequential and generation-guarded. provider.connect completes before validation, and no Promise.all fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connected providers skip provider.connect on warm state; already-loaded submenu data is reused. The diff does not alter connection state caching, recent-history caching, or failure retry behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the submenu delegate, dispatch path, sequential awaits, and boundary calls are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote connection duration varies by provider, but call cardinality and its placement after explicit child selection are clear.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The PR does not move remote connection or filesystem validation onto Enter-to-open; those boundaries remain behind a separate explicit child selection and retain cardinality one.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced submenu scheduling, construction, width/height layout, filtering, disposal, cached workspace history, and remote selection boundaries. The changes either reduce eager hover work or add bounded deliberate-activation/rendering work; no high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.
